title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
layout_note: Two task rows split by a long dashed horizontal rule: the top row (a QA task) holds the question box, two narrow baseline panels stacked on the left (Standard, Reason Only), a middle Act-Only panel and a tall method panel on the right; the bottom row (an embodied household task) holds the task box above an Act-Only panel on the left and the method panel on the right. Every panel is a full transcript of one prompting style on the same task.
grouping: Each prompting style is its own white rounded rectangle with a thin dark outline; its name sits in a light-grey rounded tab that overlaps the top edge, numbered like (1a), (1b), (2b). The method panels take the right-hand column of both rows and are the tallest. The only separator between the two tasks is the dashed rule.
shapes_depth: Flat; no fills on the panels, no shadows. All content is monospace transcript text: bold prefixes Thought N / Act N / Obs N start each line, tool verbs (Search, Finish, Think) are set in bold blue with their arguments in square brackets. Highlighter-style rectangles sit behind words: red behind wrong reasoning or failed observations, green behind the facts that lead to the answer, light blue behind the Think steps of the embodied example. A large red cross or green check in each panel's bottom-right corner gives the outcome. No arrows.
proposed_highlight: The method gets the widest, tallest panel in the right column of each row, and is the only style that interleaves Thought, Act and Obs lines; its panels end in a green check while every baseline ends in a red cross. Green highlights trace the evidence chain through its trajectory.
lesson: An agent's reasoning-acting loop can be shown with no arrows at all: print the trajectory as Thought/Act/Obs lines in monospace, colour the tool verbs, highlight right and wrong spans in green and red, and end each competing transcript with a check or a cross.
notes: elements 'other' = background highlighter marks on text spans and the outcome check/cross marks. Venue and year from the PDF first page ('Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2023').

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: interleaved reasoning and acting with LLM prompting

core.what: prompting styles as side-by-side transcript panels per task, baselines left and the tall ReAct panel rightmost: HotpotQA row (Standard, CoT, Act-Only, then ReAct) above a dashed rule, AlfWorld row (Act-Only, then ReAct) below, each panel ending in a red cross or a green check

relations.form: each prompting style is a white rounded panel with a grey numbered tab title (1a)-(1d), (2a)-(2b); the ReAct panels sit at the right of each row and are the tallest
each row opens with one task box (the HotpotQA question, the AlfWorld room description) above the panels that all answer it
inside the panels the agent loop is written as numbered Thought/Act/Obs lines stacked top to bottom, unrolled step by step rather than drawn as a cycle
a long horizontal dashed rule splits the figure into two task rows with the same left-baseline / right-ReAct arrangement

channels.colour: highlighter colour = role of a span: red = wrong reasoning or failed observation, green = facts leading to the answer, blue = Think steps (and bold blue = tool verbs Search/Finish/Think); red cross vs green check marks outcome; blue carries two meanings (tool verb text and Think-step highlight)
channels.shape: rounded panels = one prompting method's transcript; tab labels = method names; everything inside is monospace text
channels.line: no arrows; one dashed rule between task rows
channels.frame: each rounded panel = one method on one task

quality.strengths: data is drawn as data - real question, real transcripts - and highlights trace the story (where the baselines go wrong in red, which retrieved facts the ReAct chain uses in green) so the outcome is checkable; baselines and ReAct are placed in parallel panels with ReAct last; outcome icons give the 5 s answer
quality.weaknesses: the figure is almost entirely text, so the Thought/Act/Obs loop - the method - is never drawn as structure; panels differ in size and are packed irregularly (Standard and CoT stacked beside Act-Only), so the comparison is not identical panels; long transcripts make the 30 s read hard; blue does double duty

insights.structure: Two task rows split by a long dashed rule: HotpotQA on top (question box, stacked Standard and CoT panels, Act-Only panel, tall ReAct panel on the right) and AlfWorld below (task box over Act-Only on the left, ReAct on the right); each prompting style is a white rounded panel with a grey tab title numbered (1a)-(2b).
insights.data: Everything is monospace transcript text with bold Thought/Act/Obs prefixes, tool verbs (Search, Finish, Think) in bold blue with bracketed arguments.
insights.emphasis: Highlighter rectangles mark the story: red behind wrong reasoning or failed observations, green behind the facts leading to the answer, blue behind Think steps; red crosses vs green checks in each panel corner give outcomes, and ReAct always takes the right-hand, tallest panel.
insights.flow: Read top to bottom inside each transcript, left to right across baselines to the method; no arrows at all.
insights.avoid: Dense small monospace text makes it a reading figure rather than a diagram; it only works at full page width.

arrangement.units: white rounded transcript panels with overlapping grey title tabs, arranged in two task rows
arrangement.inputs_as: question/task text box at the top of each row
